<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/ARCHITECTURE.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/ARCHITECTURE.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0eca80a707822bf635b43ee6347109a87f48c0af` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6890bbbb2ef8d1578526edc83fcfc96718710747` — the merge of head `31c4e6b6a0270ae483c6ea7dce3f52e17910abdd` into base `0eca80a707822bf635b43ee6347109a87f48c0af`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6890bbbb2ef8d1578526edc83fcfc96718710747 && git checkout 6890bbbb2ef8d1578526edc83fcfc96718710747
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0eca80a707822bf635b43ee6347109a87f48c0af 31c4e6b6a0270ae483c6ea7dce3f52e17910abdd && git checkout -B drift-repro 0eca80a707822bf635b43ee6347109a87f48c0af && git merge --no-ff 31c4e6b6a0270ae483c6ea7dce3f52e17910abdd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0eca80a707822bf635b43ee6347109a87f48c0af
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对

ACCEPT at `Head-sha: 31c4e6b6a0270ae483c6ea7dce3f52e17910abdd` (2026-11-10T15:18Z).

- **Shape:** a no-card order from the security#1 seat, in two rounds. A contract-tier reviewer approved the order with ten edits before dispatch. Round 2 applied the PR review's edits: foreign-session and address-change pins, a fail-closed reading of an unreadable session token, one published TSDoc sentence in `@objectstack/client`, and the body's known-and-deliberate line. 8 files, +853 / −7. Not governed (`check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 32236`: 0 of 8 paths). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, BREAKING, patch, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` · `Metadata-protocol: none` · `Skills-docs: none`. The title carries `!`.
- **Rule:** an account with an enrolled second factor is signed in by no one-time code or sign-in link alone; a code or link door asks for the second factor, as password sign-in does.
- **Premise measured:**
  - Before the change, the three code and link doors issued a full session to an enrolled account (reproduced on a real `AuthManager` rig).
  - After it, each door answers with the existing challenge and leaves no usable credential. TOTP, a backup code and a trust-device cookie complete it exactly as on the password door.
  - A session held for another account never stands in for the second factor.
  - Accounts with no enrolled factor, and door calls that issue no new session, are unchanged.
  - The vendor seam is reused by reference, with a fail-closed build assertion.
  - Ablations: seven, each red, each restored.
- **Gates:**
  - CI on this head: 58 success, with the body-guard checks re-running on the seat's body patch.
  - Locally: 100 of 100 derived commands exit 0 (`--ran`: 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN).
  - Dogfood battery on this head: `VERDICT command-exit 0`, `Tests 3711 passed`.
  - The intermediate head's red typecheck was the dev's own test type, fixed in this head.
- **Review:** the isolated contract-tier reviewer returned APPROVE-WITH-EDITS on the first head, then PASS on this head with no further edits. It probed foreign cookie, foreign bearer and garbage-cookie carriers, and none got past.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - A vendor-shaped two-factor double in `auth-manager.test.ts`, owed by the fail-closed assertion.
  - The seat widened the surface by one TSDoc sentence in `packages/client`.
  - The challenge is detected by the matcher, not by hook index.
- **Known and deliberate:** two Console screens do not read the challenge yet, and both fail closed. Their follow-up is the seat's.
- **Landing:** the seat lands it through the merge queue (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`).
